exam.title: Cloud Digital Leader
exam.study_prerequisites: No formal prerequisite. Build cloud and business literacy across transformation, networking/service models, governed data, AI and agents, workload modernization, identity/security, cost governance, observability, reliability, and SRE concepts. Use hands-on exercises to make service-selection boundaries concrete.

Innovating with Google Cloud Artificial Intelligence (~18%)

review.notes: All six August 12, 2026 domains are mapped through outcome, requirement, service/control selection, ownership, validation and operations, with three integrated scenarios, eight labs and 36 original checks. All ten guide URLs are cataloged: eight reachable and O'Reilly plus Udemy automation-blocked; none missing or broken. The older HTML guide and pre-August learning gap are explicit. No proprietary course material, question bank or recalled exam item is used.

findings.title: Agent Platform and employee app have distinct roles
findings.evidence: The April announcement identifies Agent Platform as the developer platform evolving Vertex AI and the app as the employee interface.
findings.recommendation: Separate developer lifecycle from employee discovery/use; explain that workflow building and grounding need not train model weights.
findings.resolution: Separate developer lifecycle from employee discovery/use; explain that workflow building and grounding need not train model weights.

findings.title: Cloud Run has multiple execution forms
findings.evidence: Current overview describes services, completion jobs, worker pools and singleton instances; worker scaling differs from service scaling.
findings.recommendation: Correct request-only description and qualify additional forms as current product context, not newly added exam objectives.
findings.resolution: Correct request-only description and qualify additional forms as current product context, not newly added exam objectives.

findings.title: Archive access and minimum storage duration are different decisions
findings.evidence: Archive is online with low-latency access; cold-class minimum durations concern billing and a new default class does not change existing objects.
findings.recommendation: Add access, minimum-duration/retention and existing-object distinctions.
findings.resolution: Add access, minimum-duration/retention and existing-object distinctions.

findings.title: Autoclass is management with separate rules and pricing
findings.evidence: Autoclass manages class transitions, defaults to Nearline terminal class, leaves small objects Standard and has distinct fees.
findings.recommendation: Separate the feature from individual storage classes; qualify pricing and transition details.
findings.resolution: Separate the feature from individual storage classes; qualify pricing and transition details.

findings.title: NoSQL does not imply eventual default reads
findings.evidence: Firestore documents strong default reads and ACID writes.
findings.recommendation: Teach data model versus operation/consistency choice without assuming every NoSQL service behaves alike.
findings.resolution: Teach data model versus operation/consistency choice without assuming every NoSQL service behaves alike.

findings.title: A narrower child allow grant does not subtract inherited access
findings.evidence: Effective allow policies are the union of parent and resource grants, with deny policies a separate consideration.
findings.recommendation: Add an inherited Editor/child Viewer counterexample and separate constraints from grants.
findings.resolution: Add an inherited Editor/child Viewer counterexample and separate constraints from grants.

findings.title: Detection and model refusal do not prove integration enforcement
findings.evidence: Inspect-only allows processing; inspect-and-block supplies a verdict honored by the integration; model refusal may occur independently.
findings.recommendation: Require correlated logs and downstream behavior plus allowed and blocked controls, without claiming a live test.
findings.resolution: Require correlated logs and downstream behavior plus allowed and blocked controls, without claiming a live test.

findings.title: Preview spend caps change an overly broad budget rule
findings.evidence: Current preview can pause new eligible-service use within one project; estimated costs, delays, in-flight and fixed costs prevent an exact account-wide ceiling.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish alerts-only budgets from preview caps, describe limits and manual lifting, and execute only fictional arithmetic.
findings.resolution: Distinguish alerts-only budgets from preview caps, describe limits and manual lifting, and execute only fictional arithmetic.

findings.title: DWS billing depends on mode and date
findings.evidence: Flex-start is usage based; Calendar mode charges the reserved duration; rates are scheduled to change in November 2026.
findings.recommendation: Teach start-time/commitment tradeoffs without embedding volatile rates or treating DWS as Spot.
findings.resolution: Teach start-time/commitment tradeoffs without embedding volatile rates or treating DWS as Spot.

blog_intake.value: Clarify developer Agent Platform versus employee app and relationship to older Vertex AI naming.
blog_intake.limits: Full public article read; adopted naming context only, not all feature availability, security or performance claims.

local_validation.execution_boundary: Standard-library arithmetic with fictional request and cost inputs. No Google Cloud API, provider SLO evaluator, billing forecast, spend cap, notification or real invoice was accessed.

limitations: Same-context AI review; independent human review pending.
All eight complete decision labs remain proposed. Only the exact public Python arithmetic worksheet was executed, with 26 checks.

No cloud account, project, API, model, IAM policy, workload, budget, spend cap, notification, billing control or real invoice was accessed or changed. No Google Cloud enforcement, capacity, storage, reliability or restore behavior was validated live.
The SLI, unit-cost and forecast examples use fictional inputs and explicit assumptions; they are not implementations of Google provider services.
Spend caps are preview and scoped; DWS prices change over time. Extra Cloud Run forms are current product context, not additions to the accepted August exam scope.

Google Skills course durations and YouTube/sample-form content were not fully exposed; blocked OReilly/Udemy metadata remains explicitly unverified. Public Coursera outlines were read, but no paid lessons, labs, sample questions or proprietary assessment items were accessed.
Two initially guessed documentation paths returned missing; corrected official paths were fetched successfully. Failed attempts remain in the operational receipt.
